Yes, medical students can contribute significantly to quality assurance (QA) programs in day surgery. In fact, our study confirms that students are able to identify Quality Assurance (QA) issues and propose solutions. We recommend that students have a formally recognized place in day surgery QA programs, which will enable them to play an active role in ensuring the high standards of care that patients expect from their healthcare providers.

By contributing to QA programs, medical students can:

1. Identify potential QA issues: Students can identify areas where quality can be improved and propose solutions, helping to ensure that patients receive high-quality care.
2. Develop important skills: Participating in QA programs helps develop essential skills such as critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication.
3. Enhance patient safety: By contributing to QA programs, students can help to identify and mitigate risks, ultimately leading to better patient outcomes.

It's worth noting that our study also highlights the importance of providing students with opportunities to learn from experienced colleagues in day surgery QA programs. This can include participating in clinical rotations, shadowing experienced surgeons or QA specialists, and working on quality improvement projects.

Overall, incorporating medical students into day surgery QA programs will not only enhance patient safety but also provide them with valuable learning experiences that can benefit their future careers as healthcare professionals.
